meta.title: Invalid code generated when using "Remove all the unused imports"
meta.fix_ref: rust-lang/rust-analyzer#16185 (fix: remove wrong comma after remove unnecessary braces)
meta.build_notes: GitHub release assets rust-analyzer-aarch64-apple-darwin.gz of the weekly tags 2023-12-18 and 2023-12-25; git tag --contains puts the fix first in 2023-12-25. The sysroot is the local rustup toolchain (rustc 1.98.1).
meta.notes: After removing the unused A and C, the braces around the remaining single tree were removed without its trailing comma (introduced by #16066), producing 'use m::\n    x::B,\n;'.

settings_note: The issue names no settings; the session keeps checkOnSave off (native analysis only).

files.note: a binary crate around the snippet (package name, version, edition 2021)

repro.steps: Open src/main.rs. On the use item 'use m::{ x::{A, B}, y::C, };' (cursor on the path, line 10, character 4) apply 'Remove all the unused imports'. Reported: 'use m::' / 'x::B,' / ';', which is invalid. Probe: the edited text must have no parse error that the original did not have.

attempts.summary: Run 2026-09-23T09:38 (this case revision): not-reproduced-pre. The pre build 2023-12-18 removed the unused imports without the brace removal ('x::{B},' stays inside 'use m::{ ... };', valid), the post build 2023-12-25 removed the braces correctly ('use m::' / 'x::B' / ';'). The automatic brace removal that caused the bug came with #16066 (merged 2023-12-20, first in 2023-12-25), the fix #16185 merged 2023-12-23 (also first in 2023-12-25): the bug existed only in nightly builds between the two (the reporter used 0.4.1778 and wrote 'it isn't broken on the stable release'). No weekly release has the bug (pre-check 1); no second attempt.
attempts.verdict: not-reproduced-pre (no released build with the bug)
